desc:
A region has n towns numbered 0 to n - 1, joined by two-way roads: edges[i] = [a, b] is a road between towns a and b. The towns listed in shelters have a storm shelter.

Return an array ans of length n where ans[v] is the smallest number of roads you must drive to get from town v to any town with a shelter (0 for a shelter town itself), or -1 if no shelter can be reached from v.

n = 6, edges = [[0,1], [1,2], [2,3], [4,5]], shelters = [0, 3]
-> [0, 1, 1, 0, -1, -1]
constraints: 0 ≤ edges.length ≤ 3,000; no road joins a town to itself and no pair is listed twice
0 ≤ shelters.length ≤ n; the shelter towns are distinct
hints: Running a separate BFS from every town would be O(n · (n + m)). Think about which towns the searches should start from instead.
Reverse the question: BFS from the shelters, and the level in which a town is reached is its distance to the closest shelter.
Put all shelters into the queue at distance 0 at once. Towns that are never reached keep the value -1.
editorial: Roads are two-way, so the distance from a town to its nearest shelter equals the shortest distance from the set of shelters to the town. Initialise ans with -1, set it to 0 for every shelter and enqueue them all. Then run an ordinary BFS: when you pop a town, give every neighbour whose answer is still -1 the value ans[town] + 1 and enqueue it.

Because the queue always holds towns in nondecreasing distance, the first assignment to a town is its smallest possible distance, so the value -1 doubles as the visited flag. Time O(n + m), and towns in components without a shelter are simply never touched.
